title: My first Roblox game
author: GrimReio
selftext:
https://i.redd.it/gbyl8547cvzh1.png

AI wrote 50k lines of my Roblox game in a week. Turns out that was the easy part.

For the last 9 days I’ve been building Penguin Sumo with Claude Code. Penguins bump each other off melting ice with their bellies, the ice cracks under you, and a megalodon eats whoever falls in.

The AI part went better than I expected. Claude was hooked into Roblox Studio through MCP, so it ran the game, read the errors and fixed them itself. In 9 days we got:

* 379 commits, \~30k lines of game code
* 5 arenas, 6 game modes, random events (black hole, kraken, tsunami), 84 skins you hatch from eggs
* 11 languages, phone / PC / console

Then I put $140 into Roblox ads:

* 1.5M impressions
* 6,800 plays (about 0.45%, roughly 2 cents a play)
* two thirds of new players never got to their second fight
* on phones, which are half the players, a third left during the tutorial

https://i.redd.it/gn805bqddvzh1.png

So the game didn’t take off. And the more I look at it, the less I think the problem is "the game is bad". I think "the game is the wrong shape for Roblox".

**Roblox players want a loop, not a match.** The big games right now are about collecting, growing, stealing, +1 every second. You log in to watch a number go up. My game is a 2-minute brawl. Great with friends, pointless alone at 11pm on your phone.

**The algorithm rewards playtime, and party games have short sessions by design.** A good round of Penguin Sumo is over fast. That’s the fun part, and also exactly what Roblox doesn’t push.

**Skill-based fun is a hard sell to a 10 year old on a phone.** Getting bonked into the sea in your first fight is hilarious to me. To a new player it’s "I lost, bye."

Friends make it work, and most players come in alone. With bots it’s fine. With 4 people it’s a completely different game, and almost nobody gets to see that version.

https://i.redd.it/sr8ebpjodvzh1.png

I don’t regret building it. AI made it possible to find this out in 9 days and $140 instead of 6 months. It just told me something I didn’t want to hear: you can make something fun and still build the wrong thing for the platform.

Anyway, I’ve already started a new game, so don’t worry, there will be more failures for you to enjoy. This time I’m going to check what Roblox actually wants before writing 30k lines. Probably.

If anyone here has hit the same wall (made something fun, wrong platform), I’d love to hear what you did next.

comments.author: SeasawPhilosopher
comments.body: Nice report, sadly I think you’ll find the only way to make a successful Roblox game is to add mechanics that exploit children like addictive grind loops with impossible objects that require spending Robux. I’ve played enough of these games with my sister’s kids to see the kind of patterns used and it’s why I have zero desire to develop for the platform.
